Introducing {risAT}: Working with the Austrian Legal Information System RIS

Austria
[object Object]

{risAT} is an R package that wraps the Austrian RIS (Rechtsinformationssystem) Open Government Data API, making it easier to work with Austrian jurisprudence in R.

Author

Roland Schmidt

Published

30 Jun 2026

Modified

12 Jul 2026

1 Context & Purpose

The Austrian Legal Information System, RIS, short for Rechtsinformationssystem, is the central public repository of Austrian law and jurisprudence. Broadly speaking, it provides access to Austria’s current and historical legal norms, including federal and state law, as well as to the jurisprudence of the country’s most important courts and judicial institutions. The latter covers the case law of the Constitutional Court (Verfassungsgerichtshof, VfGH), the Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgerichtshof, VwGH), the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, BVwG), and decisions by institutions such as the Equal Treatment Commission, the Data Protection Authority, and the Federal Disciplinary Board.

This wealth of information makes RIS an indispensable source for anyone working on issues related to the Austrian legal system. While accessing the data is straightforward via the official website, accessing RIS data in bulk and analyzing it beyond individual cases has mostly required tinkering with the service’s API and wrangling the returned JSON results. The new R package {risAT} aims to lower this barrier by providing an intuitive and efficient way to work with RIS data and make it amenable to analysis beyond the single case. The package wraps the RIS Open Government Data REST API and returns tidy tibbles with standardized English column names, while preserving the links and metadata needed to inspect the original RIS records. With this, {risAT} can be helpful to researchers, students, and journalists who work in R and are interested in the Austrian legal framework. {risAT} can serve, e.g., as a starting point for text mining and text analysis when collecting the required corpus; similarly, the package can be used to produce descriptive statistics on the frequency of specific decisions by a particular court and how this frequency has developed over time. Whenever you are interested in more than one case, {risAT} can come handy.

Please note that the package is still under development (0.0.1) and that its interface may change. Furthermore, the package is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by RIS or the Austrian Federal Chancellery.

You can install {risAT} from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("werkstattcodes/{risAT}")

For the full function reference, see the documentation site and the GitHub repository. If you want to receive updates on releases, I would recommend subscribing to the repo on Github. For any questions or suggestions, please use the discussion board or file an issue on the GitHub page.

And you if you use the package in a publication, please cite it as follows:

2 Scope

The RIS API organises case law by application. In practice, that means one application for each court system or specialised decision-making body. {risAT} provides convenience wrappers for the main courts, plus a generic search function:

Function Court / Body
ris_search_vfgh() Constitutional Court (Verfassungsgerichtshof, VfGH)
ris_search_vwgh() Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgerichtshof, VwGH)
ris_search_justiz() Ordinary courts (OGH, OLG, LG, BG)
ris_search_bvwg() Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, BVwG)
ris_search_lvwg() State administrative courts (Landesverwaltungsgerichte, LVwG)
ris_search_dsk() Data protection authorities
ris_search_dok() Disciplinary body decisions
ris_search_pvak() Staff representation oversight
ris_search_gbk() Equal Treatment Commission (Gleichbehandlungskommission)
ris_search_case_law() Generic wrapper for any supported case-law application

The court-specific functions are thin wrappers around ris_search_case_law().

Every result includes standard columns such as id, application, decision_date, case_number, and document_type. It also includes list-columns such as content_urls, which stores links to the RIS HTML and PDF records.

With echo = TRUE, {risAT} prints the equivalent RIS web search URL and the number of returned rows. This is useful because it lets you move between the reproducible R workflow and the browser interface that many legal researchers already know.

3 Examples

The examples below are meant to show the kinds of questions one can start asking once RIS case law is available as data. They are not full analyses, and the query choices are intentionally transparent so that they can be adjusted for more careful research designs.

3.1 VfGH - European Convention on Human Rights

To start with, let’s use {risAT} to query the data on the decisions of the Austrian Constitutional Court, the Verfassungsgerichtshof (VfGH). Considering the special status of the European Convention for Human Rights (ECHR; it is directly applicable in Austria), I was wondering how frequently the VfGH refers to norms of the ECHR in its decisions. To answer this, the code below

  1. retrieves the meta data on all decisions of the VfGH from the beginning of 2000 to the end of 2025, and
  2. checks whether the ECHR is referenced among the norms invoked in each of the decisions. The norms column, returned by the API, stipulates the norms in question.
Code 
vfgh_2000_2025 %>%
  count(document_type)
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   document_type     n
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 Rechtssatz     9681
## 2 Text          11319

library(janitor)
janitor::get_dupes(vfgh_2000_2025, id)
## # A tibble: 0 × 32
## # ℹ 32 variables: id <chr>, dupe_count <int>, application <chr>,
## #   authority <chr>, document_url <chr>, document_type <chr>,
## #   case_number <list>, norms <list>, decision_date <date>, keywords <chr>,
## #   ecli <chr>, vfgh_decision_type <chr>, vfgh_court <chr>,
## #   vfgh_indices <list>, vfgh_collection_number <chr>,
## #   judikatur_vfgh_entscheidungstexte <chr>, content_urls <list>,
## #   app_metadata <list>, vfgh_decision_text_case_number <chr>, …
janitor::get_dupes(vfgh_2000_2025, case_number)
## # A tibble: 17,347 × 32
##    case_number dupe_count id    application authority document_url document_type

Here is the relevant function call via {risAT}’s ris_search_vfgh()1:

1 This call is rather comprehensive and can be quite time consuming. To add a layer of robustness, you may want to split it into separate calls for each year, store the interim results, and then combine them. Also a note on the netiquette: The RIS API is a public service, and it is important to avoid overloading it with too many requests in a short time. Please be considerate and avoid sending too many requests in quick succession.

Get all decisions by the Constitutional Court (VfGH) 
vfgh_2000_2025 <- ris_search_vfgh(
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
)

In total we get data on 21000 decisions. Below is a glimpse of the data structure, which shows the main columns and their types. The norms column is a list-column, which means that each row can contain multiple norms.

In the next step, let’s check which of the decisions obtained above make reference to the ECHR and calculate the annual totals of decisions with and without such a reference. The code below extracts the year from the decision_date column, checks for ECHR references in the norms column, and calculates annual totals and shares.

To avoid duplicates, we only look at the decisions of type “text”, and not “Rechtssatz” (which is summary of the legal essence of a decision).

Identify VfGH decisions with ECHR norm reference 
class(vfgh_2000_2025$norms)
## [1] "list"
table(vfgh_2000_2025$document_type)
## 
## Rechtssatz       Text 
##       9681      11319

#keep only decisions of type "Text"
vfgh_2000_2025_echr <- vfgh_2000_2025 %>%
  filter(document_type=="Text") 

nrow(vfgh_2000_2025_echr)  
## [1] 11319


#extract year; check for ECHR reference in norms
#add dummy TRUE if norms (list) contains at least one reference to the EMRK
vfgh_2000_2025_echr <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  mutate(year=year(decision_date)) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_echr = map_lgl(norms, \(x) any(str_detect(as.character(unlist(x)), fixed("EMRK")), na.rm = TRUE))
  )

#calculate annual totals (and labels for later plotting)
vfgh_year <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  count(year, norm_echr) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_reference = factor(
      if_else(norm_echr, "Norm references ECHR", "General decisions"),
      levels = c("Norm references ECHR", "General decisions")
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    share = n / total,
    echr_label = if_else(norm_echr, scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1), NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

Now let’s visualize the results.

Identify VfGH decisions with ECHR norm reference 
vfgh_year_totals <- vfgh_year %>%
  distinct(year, total) %>%
  filter(total > 0)


vfgh_year %>%
ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n, fill=norm_reference)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  geom_text(
    data = vfgh_year_totals,
    aes(x = year, y = total, label = total),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.35,
    color = "black",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = echr_label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "black",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5),
  expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("General decisions" = "#1F3A5F", "Norm references ECHR" = "#D4A017"),
    name = "Norm reference"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual Constitutional Court decisions referencing the ECHR",
    subtitle = "Decisions by year, with decisions containing a norm reference to the European Convention on Human Rights highlighted.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VfGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 by decision year, highlighting decisions with a norm reference to the European Convention on Human Rights.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    legend.location = "plot",
    legend.justification.top = "left",
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

As you can see – ignoring the plotting code – only a few lines of code yield a clear picture on the presence of the EMRK in decisions of the Austrian Constitutional Court. The graph above shows the annual number of decisions by the VfGH, highlighting those which contain a norm reference to the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). Both the number and the share of decisions referencing the ECHR have increased over time, with a notable surge in recent years.

We can further refine the analysis by looking at the actual paragraphs of the ECHR which are referenced in the decisions. The code below extracts the article and paragraph numbers from the norms column, counts the occurrences of each combination, and displays the results.

Code 

vfgh_2000_2025_echr <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  filter(norm_echr==TRUE) %>% #keep only decisions with at least one norm reference to the ECHR
  mutate(norms=map(norms, normalise_norm_values)) %>% #standardize the norms column (elements of differnt class)
  unnest_longer(norms) #unnest

class(vfgh_2000_2025_echr$norms)
## [1] "character"

echr_decisions_total <- n_distinct(vfgh_2000_2025_echr$id)

echr_norm_names <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ZP_type, ~art, ~norm_short,
  NA_character_, "1", "Respect for human rights",
  NA_character_, "2", "Right to life",
  NA_character_, "3", "Prohibition of torture",
  NA_character_, "4", "Slavery and forced labour",
  NA_character_, "5", "Liberty and security",
  NA_character_, "6", "Fair trial",
  NA_character_, "7", "No punishment without law",
  NA_character_, "8", "Private and family life",
  NA_character_, "9", "Thought, conscience and religion",
  NA_character_, "10", "Expression",
  NA_character_, "11", "Assembly and association",
  NA_character_, "12", "Marriage",
  NA_character_, "13", "Effective remedy",
  NA_character_, "14", "Discrimination",
  NA_character_, "15", "Emergency derogation",
  NA_character_, "16", "Political activity of aliens",
  NA_character_, "17", "Abuse of rights",
  NA_character_, "18", "Use of restrictions",
  "1. ZP", "1", "Property",
  "1. ZP", "2", "Education",
  "1. ZP", "3", "Free elections",
  "4. ZP", "1", "No imprisonment for debt",
  "4. ZP", "2", "Freedom of movement",
  "4. ZP", "3", "No expulsion of nationals",
  "4. ZP", "4", "Collective expulsion",
  "6. ZP", "1", "Abolition of death penalty",
  "7. ZP", "1", "Expulsion safeguards",
  "7. ZP", "2", "Criminal appeal",
  "7. ZP", "3", "Wrongful conviction",
  "7. ZP", "4", "Double jeopardy",
  "7. ZP", "5", "Spousal equality",
  "12. ZP", "1", "General discrimination",
  "13. ZP", "1", "Death penalty abolition"
)

norm_count <- vfgh_2000_2025_echr %>%
  filter(str_detect(norms, regex("EMRK"))) %>% #keep only EMRK norms
  mutate(
    ZP=str_detect(norms, regex("ZP")), #identify references to an additional protocol of th ECHR
    ZP_type=str_extract(norms, regex("\\d\\.?\\s+ZP"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_split=str_split(norms, regex(",s*")) #split norm if it contains multiple artiles
  ) %>%
  unnest_longer(norm_split) %>% 
  mutate(art=str_extract(norm_split, regex("(?<=Art)\\d+")))  %>% #extract article
  mutate(abs=str_extract(norm_split, regex("(?<=Abs)\\d+")))   %>% #extract paragraph
  distinct(id, ZP_type, art, abs) %>%
  count(ZP_type, art, abs, sort=T) %>%
  mutate(label=str_squish(str_c(
    coalesce(str_c(ZP_type, ", "), ""),
    coalesce(str_c("Art. ", art), ""),
    coalesce(str_c(", Abs. ", abs), "")
  ))) %>%
  left_join(echr_norm_names, by = join_by(ZP_type, art)) %>%
  mutate(norm_short = coalesce(norm_short, "ECHR norm"))
Plot the most frequent ECHR norm references 

norm_count_top <- norm_count %>%
  mutate(label = forcats::fct_lump_n(label, n = 10, w = n, other_level = "all other ECHR norms referenced.")) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(n),
    norm_short = if_else(
      n_distinct(norm_short) == 1,
      first(norm_short),
      "Other ECHR norms"
    ),
    .by = label
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rel = n / echr_decisions_total,
    bar_label = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", n, rel * 100),
    label = forcats::fct_reorder(label, n),
    label = forcats::fct_relevel(label, "all other ECHR norms referenced.", after = 0)
  )

left_axis_labels <- norm_count_top %>%
  mutate(
    label_md = str_c(
      # escape leading "1." etc. so gridtext doesn't parse it as an ordered list
      str_replace_all(str_wrap(as.character(label), 15), "\n", "<br>") |>
        str_replace("^(\\d+)\\.", "\\1\\\\."),
      if_else(
        label == "all other ECHR norms referenced.",
        "", # short name would be redundant here
        str_c(
          "<br><span style='font-size:8pt;color:#52616B'>(",
          str_replace_all(str_wrap(norm_short, 22), "\n", "<br>"),
          ")</span>"
        )
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  { setNames(.$label_md, as.character(.$label)) }

vfgh_decisions_total <- sum(vfgh_year$n)
echr_share <- echr_decisions_total / vfgh_decisions_total

norm_count_top %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = label)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1F3A5F", width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = bar_label),
    hjust = -0.15,
    color = "#263238",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.18)))+
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) left_axis_labels[x]) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Which norms of the European Convention on Human Rights does the Austrian Constitutional Court reference most often?",
    subtitle = str_glue(
      "Between 2000 and 2025, the Austrian Constitutional Court (VfGH) issued ",
      "{scales::comma(vfgh_decisions_total)} decisions. ",
      "{scales::comma(echr_decisions_total)} of them ({scales::percent(echr_share, accuracy = 0.1)}) ",
      "contain a norm reference to the ECHR. The chart shows the most frequently referenced ",
      "Convention norms; percentages give the share of ECHR-referencing decisions citing each norm. "
    ),
    x = "Number of decisions",
    y = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("Most frequently referenced ECHR norms in Austrian Constitutional Court decisions from 2000 to 2025. Numbers include also references to ECHR Additional Protocols. Short names of the referenced Convention rights are shown in parentheses below each norm.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    # must target the leaf element: with ggplot2 4.0 complete themes,
    # axis.text.y gets overridden by the theme's plain axis.text.y.left
    axis.text.y.left = ggtext::element_markdown(
      size = gg_axis_size,
      family = gg_plot_family,
      color = "#263238",
      lineheight = 1.3,
      hjust = 1, # place the label box against the axis
      halign = 1 # right-align lines inside the box
    ),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#D8DEE4", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

3.2 VwGH - Subsidiary Protection

Let’s move on to the next court – the Verwaltungsgerichtshof (VwGH), Austria’s highest court on administrative matters.

An item which has been high on the political and wider public agenda is the question of asylum and migration. As the highest court for administrative matters, the VwGH is the final instance for decisions on asylum and migration. Here, I want to demonstrate how to use the {risAT} package to query jurisprudence for a specific legal norm. The norm parameter in the function allows the user to search for decisions which cite a specific legal norm. In this example, I will search for decisions which cite AsylG 2005 §8, the provision on subsidiary protection.

Get VwGH data on subsidiary protection 
asyl_subsidiary_all <- ris_search_vwgh(
  norm = "'AsylG 2005 §8'",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_legal_principles = F,
  echo = TRUE
)

#check for duplicates
nrow(janitor::get_dupes(asyl_subsidiary_all, id))
## [1] 0
glimpse(asyl_subsidiary_all)

## $ keywords                            <list> NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, "Anzuwendende…
## $ vwgh_collection_number              <chr> NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA…

The resulting graph shows the annual number of decisions by the VwGH which cite AsylG 2005 §8 (subsidiary protection). The number of decisions citing this norm has been increasing over time, with a notable surge in the early 2020s.

Plot data on subsidiary protection by year 
asyl_by_year <- asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  mutate(year = year(decision_date)) |>
  distinct(year, id) %>%
  count(year, name = "decisions") |>
  complete(year = 2000:2025, fill = list(decisions = 0L)) |>
  arrange(year)

asyl_by_year |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2F6F73", width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(
    data = asyl_by_year |> filter(decisions > 0),
    aes(label = decisions),
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of decisions by the Austrian Administrative Court (VwGH) referring to 'AsylG 2005 §8' (subsidiary protection)",
    subtitle = "Decisions from 2000 to 2025; Graph reveals a surge of decisions in the wake of the Syrian refugee 'crisis'.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VwGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 citing AsylG 2005 section 8 by decision year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()

3.2.1 Query parameter to investigate countries

The graph above shows all decisions pertaining to the norm AsylG 2005 §8. We can also combine the search for a specific norm with a free text search query, which allows to further narrow down the results. In the example below, I add the search term Afghan* OR Syri* OR Irak* to capture decisions which relate to Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq.

Query subsidiary protection decisions related to Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq 
asyl_subsidiary_afghan_syria <- ris_search_vwgh(
  norm = "'AsylG 2005 §8'",
  query="Afghan* OR Syri* OR Irak*",
  decision_date_from = "2000-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = T,
  search_legal_principles = F,
  echo = TRUE
)

afghan_syria_ids <- as.character(asyl_subsidiary_afghan_syria$id)

asyl_subsidiary_all <- asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  mutate(
    year = year(decision_date),
    afghan_syria = as.character(id) %in% afghan_syria_ids
  ) 
  
asyl_by_year <- asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  distinct(year, id, afghan_syria) |>
  count(year, afghan_syria, name = "decisions") |>
  complete(
    year = 2000:2025,
    afghan_syria = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    fill = list(decisions = 0L)
  ) |>
  arrange(year, afghan_syria)

asyl_by_year_labels <- asyl_by_year |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    total = sum(decisions),
    afghan_syria_decisions = sum(decisions[afghan_syria]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

asyl_by_year_segment_labels <- asyl_by_year |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(
    total = sum(decisions),
    afghan_syria_pct = if_else(total > 0, decisions / total, NA_real_),
    afghan_syria_label = if_else(
      afghan_syria & decisions > 0,
      scales::percent(afghan_syria_pct, accuracy = 1),
      NA_character_
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()
Plot subsidiary protection decisions by year and country group 
asyl_by_year |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill=afghan_syria)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  geom_text(
    data = asyl_by_year_labels |> filter(total > 0),
    aes(x = year, y = total, label = total),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = asyl_by_year_segment_labels,
    aes(label = afghan_syria_label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    size = gg_annot_size,
    family = gg_plot_family,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2000, 2025, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "#2F6F73", "TRUE" = "#A6544F"),
    labels = c("FALSE" = "Other", "TRUE" = "Afghanistan, Syria, Iraq"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 5, colour = "white"))) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of decisions by the Austrian Administrative Court (VwGH) referring to 'AsylG 2005 §8' (subsidiary protection)",
    subtitle = "Decisions from 2000 to 2025, highlighting decisions mentioning Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("VwGH decisions from 2000 to 2025 citing AsylG 2005 section 8 by decision year, highlighting decisions related to Afghanistan, Syria, or Iraq.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()

3.3 BVwG - Asylum & Climate Change

Now let’s use the query function for a different court, the Bundesverwaltungsgericht (BVwG), the federal administrative court of first instance. Let’s again query for the presence of a search term, here ‘Klimawandel’ (climate change), in the decision text or legal principles. The query covers all years between 2014, the court’s first year in operation, up until the end of 2025.

Get all decisions by the BVwG which contain ‘Klimawandel’ 
climateChange_bvwg <- ris_search_bvwg(
  query = "Klimawandel",
  decision_date_from = "2014-01-01",
  decision_date_to = "2025-12-31",
  search_decision_text = TRUE,
  search_legal_principles = TRUE,
  echo = TRUE
)
Plot annual BVwG decisions mentioning ‘Klimawandel’ 
climateChange_bvwg %>%
  mutate(year=lubridate::year(decision_date)) %>%
  count(year) %>%
  ggplot()+
  labs(title="Annual number of decisions by the BVwG which contain 'Klimawandel'",
  x = NULL,
  y = "Number of decisions",
  caption=ris_graph_caption("Annual number of BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel'."))+
  geom_line(aes(x=year, y=n), color="#7F1D1D")+
  geom_point(aes(x=year, y=n), color="#7F1D1D")+
  geom_text(
    data = \(data) filter(data, year %in% c(2019, 2023, 2024, 2025)),
    aes(x = year, y = n, label = n),
    nudge_x = 0.15,
    hjust = 0,
    color = "black",
    family = gg_plot_family
  )+
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2015, 2020, 2025),
    limits = c(2014, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0), add = c(0, 1))
  )+
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 1))

How many of these decisions arise in an asylum context? Analogous to the ECHR example above, we can check the norms column for asylum-related norms. The table below shows, per year, the share of ‘Klimawandel’ decisions which reference such a norm.

Tabulate BVwG ‘Klimawandel’ decisions by asylum-norm reference 
climateChange_bvwg <- climateChange_bvwg |>
  mutate(year=year(decision_date)) %>%
  mutate(
    norm_asyl = map_lgl(norms, \(x) any(str_detect(as.character(unlist(x)), regex("Asyl", ignore_case=TRUE)), na.rm = TRUE))
    )

tblclimateChange_bvwg <- climateChange_bvwg %>%
  count(year, norm_asyl) %>%
  mutate(norm_asyl = if_else(norm_asyl, "asylum_norm", "other")) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = norm_asyl, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)  %>%
  complete(year = 2014:2025, fill = list(asylum_norm = 0, other = 0)) %>%
  mutate(
    total = asylum_norm + other,
    asylum_norm_rel = if_else(total > 0, asylum_norm / total, NA_real_)
  )

tblclimateChange_bvwg %>%
  select(year, total, asylum_norm_rel) %>%
  reactable(
    columns = list(
      year = colDef(name = "Year"),
      total = colDef(name = "Total decisions"),
      asylum_norm_rel = colDef(
        name = "Share with asylum norm",
        format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 1)
      )
    ),
    compact = TRUE,
    bordered = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    pagination = FALSE
  )

The same split as a chart:

Plot BVwG ‘Klimawandel’ decisions by asylum-norm reference 
tblclimateChange_bvwg %>%
  select(year, asylum_norm, other) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(asylum_norm, other),
    names_to = "decision_group",
    values_to = "decisions"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    decision_group = factor(
      decision_group,
      levels = c("other", "asylum_norm"),
      labels = c("Klimawandel, no asylum norm", "Klimawandel with asylum norm")
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill = decision_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2015, 2020, 2025),
    limits = c(2014, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Klimawandel, no asylum norm" = "#1F3A5F",
      "Klimawandel with asylum norm" = "#D4A017"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "BVwG Klimawandel decisions by asylum-norm reference",
    subtitle = "Annual decisions mentioning Klimawandel, split by whether an asylum-related norm is referenced.",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of decisions",
    caption = ris_graph_caption("BVwG decisions mentioning 'Klimawandel' by decision year and asylum-related norm reference.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme()

3.4 Equality and discrimination

The Equal Treatment Commission decisions are another useful example because the wrapper exposes domain-specific filters. Instead of only searching text, we can directly filter by discrimination ground. The chart below shows the annual absolute frequency of different discrimination grounds across all years currently available through the RIS GBK endpoint.

Search GBK decisions by discrimination ground and year 
discrimination_grounds <- c(
  gender = "Gender",
  ethnicity = "Ethnicity",
  religion = "Religion",
  worldview = "Worldview",
  age = "Age",
  sexual_orientation = "Sexual orientation",
  multiple = "Multiple discrimination"
)

gbk_topics <- tibble(
  discrimination_ground = names(discrimination_grounds),
  discrimination_grounds_en = unname(discrimination_grounds)
)


li_gbk_all <- gbk_topics$discrimination_ground |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(ground) {
    ris_search_gbk(discrimination_ground = ground, echo = TRUE)
  }) 

fn_normalize_lists <- function(df) {
df %>%
  mutate(
    across(any_of(c("id", "application","authority", "document_url","gbk_commission", "gbk_discrimination_ground", "gbk_discrimination_ground_en","gbk_discrimination_offense", "gbk_decision_type", "gk_senate")), as.character),
    across(any_of(c("decision_date", "modified")), as.Date),
    across(any_of(c("norms", "content_urls", "case_number")), as.list)
    )
}

df_gbk_all <- li_gbk_all %>%
  map(., \(x) fn_normalize_lists(x)) %>%
  list_rbind(names_to = "discrimination_ground")

df_gbk_all_year <- df_gbk_all  %>%
  mutate(year = year(decision_date)) %>%
  summarise(decisions = n(), .by = c(year, discrimination_ground)) %>%
  left_join(gbk_topics, by = "discrimination_ground") %>%
  mutate(
    discrimination_grounds_en = factor(
      discrimination_grounds_en,
      levels = unname(discrimination_grounds)
    )
  )
Plot annual GBK results by discrimination ground 
gbk_plot_data <- df_gbk_all_year %>%
  mutate(ground_total = sum(decisions), .by = discrimination_grounds_en) %>%
  mutate(
    ground_share = ground_total / sum(decisions),
    facet_label = str_glue(
      "{discrimination_grounds_en}: {scales::comma(ground_total)} ({scales::percent(ground_share, accuracy = 0.1)})"
    ),
    facet_label = forcats::fct_reorder(facet_label, as.integer(discrimination_grounds_en))
  )

gbk_fill_palette <- c(
  "Gender" = "#2F6F73",
  "Ethnicity" = "#8A5A44",
  "Religion" = "#6C757D",
  "Worldview" = "#4F5D75",
  "Age" = "#9A6B2F",
  "Sexual orientation" = "#7B6D8D",
  "Multiple discrimination" = "#A6544F"
)

gbk_plot_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = decisions, fill = discrimination_grounds_en)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, key_glyph = draw_key_point) +
  facet_wrap(vars(facet_label)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)), labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gbk_fill_palette) +
  labs(
    title = "Discrimination grounds in Equal Treatment Commission decisions",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Annual RIS search results by discrimination ground, ",
      min(gbk_plot_data$year),
      " to ",
      max(gbk_plot_data$year)
    ),
    x = "Decision year",
    y = "RIS search results",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = ris_graph_caption("Equal Treatment Commission search results by discrimination ground and decision year.")
  ) +
  ris_plot_theme() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_textbox(face = "bold")
  )

4 Working with the result links

One practical detail is worth highlighting. {risAT} does not only return the fields used in the plots above; it also keeps the links to the original RIS documents. The content_urls column is a list-column. Unnesting it gives one row per available format, usually including HTML and PDF.

Unnest RIS content URLs 
asyl_subsidiary_all |>
  prepare_content_urls_table(n = 12) |>
  reactable(
    searchable = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 6,
    bordered = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    compact = TRUE
  )

This is helpful for reproducibility. The same pipeline that gets you to a plot can also keep a trace back to the official record.

5 What’s next

At the moment, {risAT} focuses on the RIS case-law and federal-law endpoints. That already covers a lot: constitutional review, administrative-law disputes, data protection, equality decisions, ordinary court case law, and more. Future work will likely involve broadening API coverage and refining some of the court-specific parameter mappings.

For now, the package is best understood as a pragmatic bridge between RIS and the R workflow: search in a way that remains close to the official system, return data in a shape that is pleasant to work with, and keep links back to the source documents. If you run into bugs or have suggestions, the issue tracker is the best place to leave them.
